title: Solar cycle
subtitle: Sunset, the crossing, and the sun that comes back as something else
question: What happens to the sun between the western horizon and the eastern one, and who says so?
period: New Kingdom compositions, drawing on much older solar material
place: Royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings; solar temples and hymns more widely
evidenceBoundary: Egyptian sources do not agree on one night journey. Each scene below names the corpus it comes from. Where the archive's material is a set of image plates rather than translated prose, that is stated.
reconstruction: The forms of the sun and the structure of the crossing come from the wiki's solar-cycle article and the Underworld Books packets. Budge's translations are more than a century old and are used only where nothing newer is in the archive.
accessibleSummary: A stepper of six stages with the same content as the animation, listing corpus, actors, and what changes at each stage.

scenes.title: Khepri at dawn
scenes.body: The morning sun is Khepri, the scarab: becoming, transformation, movement that has just started. Naming the sun three times across a day is a claim about process rather than about three separate gods.
detail: Scarab imagery marks renewal wherever it appears, including on hearts and coffins.

scenes.title: Re at noon
scenes.body: At full height the sun is Re, falcon-headed with the disk: visible power, kingship, and the light that the ordered world runs on.
detail: Re joins with other gods without displacing them. Amun-Re is the largest example.

scenes.title: Atum at evening
scenes.body: The setting sun is Atum: completion, and the creator who generated the first differentiated beings. Ending the day returns to the figure who started everything.
detail: This is why sunset is not simply loss.

scenes.title: Entering the west
scenes.body: Re enters the Duat in a bark, often ram-headed at night. The route is divided into twelve regions. Names identify beings, places, doors, and the actions each requires; knowing them is what lets the king travel too.
detail: The Amduat presents a hidden geography with the bark in a middle register.
The Book of Gates makes each division a guarded gate with a named keeper.

scenes.title: The deep hour
scenes.body: In the middle of the night the solar ba unites with the Osirian body. This is the regenerative centre of the whole system: mobility meets a preserved body, and neither works alone.
detail: The archive treats this union as the clearest statement of how the two great cycles depend on each other.

scenes.title: Apep restrained
scenes.body: The serpent Apep is bound, cut, or turned back in the later hours. He is not killed permanently. Non-order is restrained again each night, which is exactly the pattern the rest of the archive keeps showing.
detail: Restraint, not destruction, is the accurate verb.

scenes.title: Emergence
scenes.body: In the final hour beings pass through a great serpent and the renewed sun emerges as Khepri. The Book of Gates ends by composing Nun, Nut, bark, and scarab into one compact image of coming up.
detail: The cycle closes where it began, which is the definition of the problem it solves.
